summary: Pre-RED verification for #221 — signed-out / redirect to sign-in

claims.claim: guard.ts: '/' is in PUBLIC_EXACT, cited at line 38
claims.evidence: src/lib/auth/guard.ts:37 — `const PUBLIC_EXACT = new Set(['/', '/about']);` — one line earlier than cited (line 38 is inside the doc-comment block above `isProtectedPath`, not the PUBLIC_EXACT declaration). Content of the claim (that '/' sits in PUBLIC_EXACT alongside '/about') is correct; only the line number is off by one.

claims.claim: PUBLIC_EXACT / public-prefix set also covers /about, /auth/*, /invite/*
claims.evidence: src/lib/auth/guard.ts:37-46 — PUBLIC_EXACT = {'/', '/about'} (exact match); isProtectedPath() also returns false via prefix checks: `pathname.startsWith('/auth/')` (line 42), `pathname.startsWith('/invite/')` (line 43, comment: 'unauthed invite landing (later slice)'), `pathname.startsWith('/_app/')` and `/.well-known` (line 44), and any path with a file extension (line 45, asset fallback regex). Anything not matching one of these falls through to `return true` (protected) at line 46.

claims.claim: src/routes/+layout.ts lines 19-25 call resolveGuardRedirect and redirect() from it; removing '/' from PUBLIC_EXACT would make anonymous visits to / redirect to /auth/login?redirect=%2F
claims.evidence: src/routes/+layout.ts:19-25 matches exactly as cited: `const target = resolveGuardRedirect({ pathname: url.pathname, search: url.search, token, nowMs: Date.now() }); if (target) redirect(302, target);`. Tracing the logic: if '/' is removed from PUBLIC_EXACT, isProtectedPath('/') falls through none of the prefix checks (guard.ts:42-45 don't match '/') and no extension regex matches, so it returns true (protected) at guard.ts:46. resolveGuardRedirect (guard.ts:60-63) then checks isTokenValid — for an anonymous visitor (no/expired token) it returns `/auth/login?redirect=${encodeURIComponent('/')}` = '/auth/login?redirect=%2F', which +layout.ts:25 passes to SvelteKit's redirect(302, ...).

claims.claim: The loading state produces no redirect (no flash) when / becomes protected
claims.evidence: Unlike the completion-gate (src/routes/+layout.svelte:110-161), which is async and has an explicit 'loading' intermediate state, resolveGuardRedirect is a pure synchronous function fed by a synchronous localStorage read (getToken() in +layout.ts:18) — there is no intermediate 'loading' phase in this guard at all. The root `load` in +layout.ts runs before any route component mounts (ssr=false, so the app boots into the layout's load before rendering +page.svelte), and calling SvelteKit's `redirect()` inside `load` aborts the render of the target branch entirely — the 'Signed out' stub in +page.svelte (line 7000, `auth.status === 'anonymous'` branch) never mounts for an anonymous visit to '/' once '/' is removed from PUBLIC_EXACT. No flash is possible by construction.

claims.claim: The login page reads the redirect param and returns the user to / after sign-in; check for sanitization that would reject redirect=%2F
claims.evidence: src/routes/auth/login/+page.svelte:18-22 reads `page.url.searchParams.get('redirect')` (falling back to `return_to`) through `safeRedirectTarget()` (src/lib/auth/redirect.ts:4-7: `if (!raw || !raw.startsWith('/') || raw.startsWith('//')) return '/'; return raw;`) — '/' passes this check untouched (starts with '/', not '//'), so `redirect=%2F` decodes to '/' and is NOT rejected/rewritten. It's embedded into each provider href via `providerHref()` (login/+page.svelte:25-27) as `return_to=%2F`. After OAuth, src/routes/auth/callback/run-callback-exchange.ts:83 returns `redirectTo: safeRedirectTarget(decoded.return_to)` and src/routes/auth/callback/+page.svelte:18 calls `goto(outcome.redirectTo)` — so a visitor bounced from '/' does land back on '/' post-sign-in.

claims.claim: Guard spec files assert '/' is public and must be updated/inverted
claims.evidence: src/lib/auth/guard.spec.ts is the only spec file with direct assertions on this behavior, at two locations: (1) line 56, inside `isProtectedPath` describe block ('lets public + auth + asset paths through'): the loop `for (const p of ['/', '/about', '/auth/login', '/auth/callback', '/_app/immutable/x.js', '/favicon.png']) expect(isProtectedPath(p)).toBe(false);` — '/' must be removed from this array (and arguably added to the 'protects app routes' list at line 59-62, or given its own assertion of `.toBe(true)`). (2) line 84, inside `resolveGuardRedirect` describe block: `it('returns null (allowed) for a public path regardless of token', () => { expect(resolveGuardRedirect({ pathname: '/', token: null, nowMs: now })).toBeNull(); });` — this must be inverted to assert a redirect to `/auth/login?redirect=%2F` is returned instead of null. No other spec file (`redirect.spec.ts`, `session-expired.spec.ts`, `request.auth-expired.spec.ts`, layout specs, or the various `page.*-session-expired.spec.ts` files) asserts PUBLIC_EXACT/isProtectedPath('/') behavior — their uses of `'/'` are unrelated (history.replaceState reset boilerplate, or safeRedirectTarget's independent open-redirect tests which are orthogonal to guard.ts's allowlist and remain correct either way).

risks: src/routes/+layout.svelte:154-158 (completion-gate enforcement effect) has an inline comment explicitly reasoning that 'the guard's isProtectedPath puts / on the public allowlist (correct for the unauth login guard)' and therefore special-cases `path === '/'` in its own redirect condition. Once '/' is removed from PUBLIC_EXACT, isProtectedPath('/') becomes true and the explicit `path === '/'` disjunct in that condition becomes redundant (isProtectedPath(path) alone would already cover it) — the comment will read as stale/misleading unless updated, though functionally the effect still behaves correctly (redundant OR-clause is harmless, not a bug).

src/routes/+page.svelte's anonymous-branch stub (line 6998-7003, `{:else if auth.status === 'anonymous'}` rendering m.agenda_signed_out()) becomes unreachable in the live app once the layout guard redirects anonymous visitors away from '/' before the page ever mounts — but this branch is not asserted by any spec found in this scan (no spec renders +page.svelte in isolation with auth.status='anonymous' at path '/'), so no spec assertion contradicts leaving that dead branch in place; it is a cleanup opportunity, not a test-breaking one. Worth flagging to the implementer as optional follow-up rather than a hard requirement.

The issue's cited line 38 for PUBLIC_EXACT in guard.ts is off by one (actual: line 37) — likely just drift from a prior edit to the file (e.g. a comment line added/removed above); harmless for the fix itself but worth using the corrected line number in the PR description to avoid confusion during review.

All reads were read-only under ~/workspace-app; no edits, commits, or writes were made, per instructions.\n\nSummary of the fix's mechanics: removing '/' from PUBLIC_EXACT (guard.ts:37) is sufficient and self-contained to make isProtectedPath('/') return true, which makes resolveGuardRedirect emit '/auth/login?redirect=%2F' for anonymous visitors, which +layout.ts's synchronous load()+redirect() call turns into an actual SvelteKit redirect before the root layout's page slot ever renders — so the 'Signed out' stub in +page.svelte never flashes. The login page and OAuth callback round-trip the redirect/return_to='/' target correctly with no sanitization rejecting it (safeRedirectTarget only rejects non-local/protocol-relative targets, and '/' is neither). Only guard.spec.ts needs test changes: one array entry removed/moved (line 56) and one assertion inverted (line 84). No other spec file in the repo makes an assertion that would break from this change."

Every other Layer-1 code path I traced (logout, post-signin redirect, invite accept/decline, /auth/login self-redirect, nav) was already either not applicable or provably safe by tracing the actual token-persist-before-redirect ordering in the callback exchange code — none of them require changes. Layer-2 axes (multi-collective query-param survival, locale-key symmetry, rights-tier agnosticism, invite-vs-auto-provisioned loading-state race) were each traced through source and came back clean/no-op. Two non-blocking hygiene items surfaced beyond the ticket's checklist: the +layout.svelte EFFECT B comment goes stale (documentation-only, no functional break) and robots.txt still advertises '/' as crawlable. No Playwright/e2e suite exists in this repo despite being named in project stack docs, so that checklist bullet currently has zero files to touch — flag to the team if e2e coverage of the guard was expected to exist already.
